title: Canonical outside of head
description: This means that the URL in question has a canonical element specified in the HTML, but outside of the \<head>.

title: Canonical points to HTTP version
description: This means that the URL in question uses the HTTPS protocol, but the canonical URL uses HTTP.

title: Disallowed JavaScript file
description: This means that the URL in question is a JavaScript URL that is blocked by a robots.txt disallow rule.

title: Disallowed image
description: This means that the URL in question is an image URL that is blocked by a robots.txt disallow rule.
note: crawl-blocked-resources covers CSS/JS only, not image URLs.

title: Disallowed Style Sheet
description: This means that the URL in question is a style sheet URL that is blocked by a robots.txt disallow rule.

title: <head> contains a <noscript> tag, which includes an image
description: This means that the URL in question contains a \<noscript> tag in the \<head>, which includes an image reference.
note: Rule flags any non-link/style/meta content in head noscript, which includes img.

title: <head> contains invalid HTML elements
description: This means that the URL in question contains a \<noscript> tag in the \<head>, which includes invalid HTML elements.

title: Meta robots found outside of <head>
description: This means that the URL in question has meta robots specified in the HTML, but outside of the \<head>.

title: Canonical contains invalid HTML attributes
description: This means that the URL in question specifies a canonical element that contains the invalid HTML attributes hreflang, lang, media, or type.

title: HTML file size exceeds Google's 2MB limit
description: This means that the URL in question is an internal HTML page whose uncompressed file size exceeds 2MB (2,097,152 bytes), which is the maximum amount of data Googlebot will crawl for any supported file type.

title: Mismatched canonical tag in HTML and HTTP header
description: This means that the URL in question has a canonical element specified both in the HTML and in the HTTP header, where the canonical URLs differ.

title: Multiple, mismatched canonical tags
description: This means that the URL in question has a canonical element specified in multiple locations (either in the HTML, in the HTTP header, or in a combination of both), and that the canonical URLs specified are not the same.

title: Canonical is malformed or empty
description: This means that the URL in question has a canonical element specified, but the canonical URL is missing or invalid.

title: Canonical points to HTTPS version
description: This means that the URL in question uses the HTTP protocol, but the canonical URL uses HTTPS.

title: Canonical points to another canonicalized URL
description: This means that the URL in question has a canonical element whereby the canonical URL itself is also canonicalized (e.g. Page A is canonicalized to Page B, which is then canonicalized to Page C).
note: Crawl mode only: follows the canonical chain via SiteContext.pages; warns when the target is itself canonicalized elsewhere.

title: Canonical loop
description: This means that the URL in question has a canonical element whereby the canonical URL is actually canonicalized back to the original URL (e.g. Page A is canonicalized to Page B, which is then canonicalized back to Page A).
note: crawl-canonical-loop detects true A↔B loops from the crawl-level canonical map; core-canonical-loop keeps the single-page heuristic.

title: Canonical points to a disallowed URL
description: This means that the URL in question has a canonical element whereby the canonical URL is disallowed in robots.txt.
note: Crawl mode only: cross-references the canonical target against the per-URL robots.txt disallow flags.

title: Canonicalized URL is noindex, nofollow
description: This means that the URL in question is canonicalized, and also noindex,nofollow.

title: Canonical points to a noindex URL
description: This means that the URL in question has a canonical element whereby the canonical URL is noindex (e.g. Page A canonicalizes to Page B, which is noindex).
note: Crawl mode only: reads the canonical target's robots state from SiteContext.pages.

title: Canonical points to a URL that is Error (5XX)
description: This means that the URL in question has a canonical element whereby the canonical URL itself resolved in an error (5XX).
note: Rule HEAD-fetches the canonical target and fails on >=400.

title: Canonical points to a URL that is Not Found 404
description: This means that the URL in question has a canonical element whereby the canonical URL itself was Not Found (404).

title: Mismatched nofollow directives in HTML and header
description: This means that the URL in question has a nofollow directive in both the HTML and in the HTTP header, where the directives do not match.

title: Mismatched noindex directives in HTML and header
description: This means that the URL in question has a noindex directive in both the HTML and in the HTTP header, where the directives do not match.

title: URL contains a form with a GET method
description: This means that the URL in question contains a form which uses the GET method.

title: Canonical only found in rendered DOM
description: This means that the URL in question has a canonical element which is only present in the rendered DOM, and is not present in the source HTML.

title: Rendered canonical is different to HTML source
description: This means that the URL in question has a canonical element in the rendered DOM, which is different to the one in the source HTML.

title: Isolated URL - only found via a canonical
description: This means that the URL in question is isolated, as it can only be found via a canonical link.
note: Crawl mode only: per-URL discovery sources (link/canonical/redirect/sitemap/entry) recorded during the crawl.

title: Isolated URL - only found via a redirect
description: This means that the URL in question is isolated, as it can only be found via a redirect.
note: Same rule; redirect-only discovery is one of the isolation forms it reports.

title: Isolated URL - only found via a noindex,follow
description: This means that the URL in question is isolated, as it can only be found via a noindex,follow link.
note: Same rule; fails when every linking page is noindex,follow.

title: Isolated URL - only linked from other isolated URLs
description: This means that the URL in question is isolated, as it can only be found via links from other isolated URLs.
note: Same rule; one propagation pass over the isolated set catches URLs linked only from isolated pages.

title: Canonical contains superfluous HTML attributes
description: This means that the URL in question specifies a canonical element that contains attributes other than rel and href.

title: Canonical is a relative URL
description: This means that the URL in question has a canonical element which uses a relative URL.

title: Canonical points to a redirecting URL
description: This means that the URL in question has a canonical element whereby the canonical URL itself is redirected (e.g. Page A is canonicalized to Page B, which redirects to Page C).

title: Multiple nofollow directives
description: This means that the URL in question has a nofollow directive in multiple locations (e.g. in the HTML and in the HTTP header).

title: Multiple noindex directives
description: This means that the URL in question has a noindex directive in multiple locations (e.g. in the HTML and in the HTTP header).

title: Noindex in HTML and HTTP header
description: This means that the URL in question has a noindex directive in both the HTML and in the HTTP header.

title: Nofollow in HTML and HTTP header
description: This means that the URL in question has a nofollow directive in both the HTML and in the HTTP header.

title: Canonical points to homepage
description: This means that the URL in question has a canonical element which points to the homepage URL.

title: Contains possible soft 404 phrases
description: This means that the URL in question responds with a 200 status but may appear to be an error page (soft 404).

title: Canonical tag in HTML and HTTP header
description: This means that the URL in question has a canonical element specified both in the HTML and in the HTTP header.

title: Multiple canonical tags
description: This means that the URL in question has a canonical element specified in multiple locations (either in the HTML, in the HTTP header, or in a combination of both).

title: Base URL malformed or empty
description: This means that the URL in question contains a base URL which is malformed or empty.

title: Multiple, mismatched base URLs
description: This means that the URL in question contains a base URL defined more than one, using different URLs.

title: Multiple base URLs
description: This means that the URL in question contains a base URL defined more than one.

title: Canonical points to a different internal URL
description: This means that the URL in question has a canonical element pointing at another internal URL. The URL in question can therefore be described as 'canonicalized.'
note: Insight only: canonicalization is detected but never surfaced as neutral information.

title: Canonical points to external URL
description: This means that the URL in question has a canonical element pointing at an external URL (a URL on a different domain or subdomain). This is known as a 'cross-domain canonical'.
note: Insight-level rule: always passes, reports cross-domain canonicals for confirmation.

title: Has noindex and nofollow directives
description: This means that the URL in question has both noindex and nofollow directives.

title: Internal Disallowed URLs
description: This means that the URL in question is disallowed by a rule in robots.txt.
note: Conflict (disallowed + noindex) is detected; a URL that is simply disallowed is not surfaced as an insight.

title: URL only has nofollow incoming internal links
description: This means that the URL in question does not have any incoming followed links from internal URLs - only nofollow ones.
note: Crawl mode only: per-edge nofollow state from SiteContext.inboundEdgesByUrl; warns at most (insight-level).

title: <head> contains a <noscript> tag
description: This means that the URL in question contains a \<noscript> tag in the \<head>.
note: We only flag invalid noscript contents; bare presence (insight) is not reported.

title: Has link with a URL referencing LocalHost or 127.0.0.1
description: This means that the URL in question contains at least one outgoing anchor link with a URL referencing LocalHost or 127.0.0.1.

title: Has link with a URL referencing a local or UNC file path
description: This means that the URL in question contains at least one outgoing anchor link with a URL referencing a local or UNC file path.

title: Has a link with whitespace in href attribute
description: This means that the URL in question contains at least one outgoing anchor link which has trailing or leading whitespace character in the href attribute.

title: Has no outgoing links
description: This means that the URL in question does not have a single outgoing link (internal or external).
note: Superset: we flag pages with no outgoing internal links, which includes pages with no outgoing links at all.

title: Has only one followed internal linking URL
description: This means that the URL in question has only one single followed **incoming** link, from one other URL on the website.
note: Rule explicitly warns at inboundCount === 1 in crawl mode.

title: Has outgoing links with malformed href data
description: URLs that contain at least one outgoing anchor link which has malformed href data.

title: URL is orphaned and was not found by the crawler
description: This means that the URL in question is not part of the crawlable website architecture, and is considered 'orphaned.'

title: Has link to a non-HTTP protocol
description: This means that the URL in question contains at least one outgoing anchor link to a destination URL which uses a non-HTTP protocol (e.g. FTP).

title: Pagination URL has no incoming internal links
description: This means that the URL in question is declared as a pagination URL, via rel="next"/"prev" links on another URL, but which has no incoming anchor links from internal URLs (i.e. the only links they have are from the pagination link element).
note: crawl-pagination-isolated checks inbound anchors for paginated URLs (crawl mode only).

title: Only receives nofollow or links from canonicalized URLs
description: This means that the URL in question only receives incoming nofollow links, or incoming links from canonicalized URLs. In other words, the URL only receives links from URLs that do not pass Link Equity.
note: Crawl mode only: warns when no inbound edge passes link equity (all nofollow or from canonicalized-away pages).

title: Has an internal link with no anchor text
description: This means that the URL in question contains at least one outgoing anchor link which has no anchor text.

title: Has an anchored image with no alt text
description: This means that the URL in question contains anchor links to image URLs with no alt text, or no alt attribute.

title: URL receives both follow & nofollow internal links
description: This means that the URL in question has a mixture of followed and nofollowed incoming links.
note: Crawl mode only: per-edge nofollow state from SiteContext.inboundEdgesByUrl.

title: Has incoming followed links without descriptive anchor text
description: This means that the URL in question receives incoming followed links from other internal URLs, which do not use descriptive anchor text (they instead have anchor text like 'click here', go', 'here', etc...).
note: Crawl mode only: per-edge anchor text from SiteContext.inboundEdgesByUrl; warns when every followed inbound link is generic.

title: 1+ outgoing followed links with non descriptive anchor text
description: This means that the URL in question contains outgoing followed links to other internal URLs, which do not use descriptive anchor text (they instead have anchor text like 'click here', go', 'here', etc...).

title: Has a link with an empty href attribute
description: This means that the URL in question contains at least one outgoing anchor link which has an empty href attribute.

title: Has broken bookmarks
description: This means that the URL in question contains broken bookmark links to other internal pages.

title: Has link with a URL in onclick attribute
description: This means that the URL in question contains at least one outgoing anchor link with a URL in an onclick attribute.

title: Title tag is missing
description: This means that the URL in question does not have a title tag present in the HTML.

title: HTML is missing or empty
description: This means that the URL in question has no HTML on the page.

title: Title tag is empty
description: This means that the URL in question contains an empty \<title> element.
note: Explicitly fails on present-but-empty title.

title: Title tag outside of head
description: This means that the URL in question has a title tag that is not in the \<head>.

title: Broken or invalid HTML
description: This means that the URL in question has broken or invalid HTML.

title: Multiple title tags
description: This means that the URL in question contains more than one title tag.

title: Meta description outside of head
description: This means that the URL in question has a meta description that is not in the \<head>.

title: <h1> tag is missing
description: This means that the URL in question does not have a header 1 tag.

title: <h1> tag is empty
description: This means that the URL in question has a header 1 tag which has no value.
note: Explicitly fails on present-but-empty H1.

title: Images with missing alt text
description: This means that the image URL in question is referenced in pages on the website without alt text.

title: Contains Lorem Ipsum dummy text
description: This means that the URL in question contains 'Lorem Ipsum' dummy text in the body content.

title: <h1> length too short
description: This means that the URL in question has a header 1 with too few words.

title: <h1> length too long
description: This means that the URL in question has a header 1 with too many words.

title: Title tag length too short
description: This means that the URL in question has a title tag with too few characters.

title: Title tag length too long
description: This means that the URL in question has a title tag with too many characters.

title: Meta description length too short
description: This means that the URL in question has a meta description with too few characters.

title: Meta description length too long
description: This means that the URL in question has a meta description with too many characters.

title: Meta description is empty
description: This means that the URL in question has a meta description that is empty.

title: Multiple meta descriptions
description: This means that the URL in question contains more than one meta description.

title: Multiple <h1> tags
description: This means that the URL in question has multiple \<h1> elements.

title: Title and meta description are the same
description: This means that the URL in question has identical text for both the title tag and the meta description.

title: Meta description is missing
description: This means that the URL in question does not have a meta description present in the HTML.

title: Internal URL redirect broken (4XX or 5XX)
description: This means that the URL in question is an internal URL that redirected to a URL that was not accessible when reference catalog crawled the website.

title: Internal URL redirects back to itself
description: This means that the URL in question has a redirect which points back at itself (e.g. URL 1 -> URL 1).

title: External URL redirect broken (4XX or 5XX)
description: This means that the URL in question is an external URL that redirected to a URL that was not accessible when reference catalog crawled the website.
note: redirect-resource-broken fails on redirected resources (incl. external) ending 4xx/5xx; needs rendered asset data (not measured under --no-cwv).

title: Resource URL redirect broken (4XX or 5XX)
description: This means that the URL in question is a resource URL that redirected to a URL that was not accessible when reference catalog crawled the website.
note: Per-resource redirect chains from the Playwright render; not measured under --no-cwv.

title: Page resource URL redirects back to itself
description: This means that the URL in question is a resource URL that redirects back to itself in a loop (e.g. URL 1 -> URL 1), which results in the resource being inaccessible.
note: Per-resource redirect loop detection from the rendered asset data; not measured under --no-cwv.

title: Page resource URL is part of a chained redirect loop
description: This means that the URL is question is a page resource URL that is part of a redirect chain which results in a redirect loop (e.g. URL 1 -> URL -> 2 -> URL 3 -> URL 1), which results in the resource being inaccessible.
note: Same rule; any loop back to a URL already in the chain is detected.

title: Internal URL is part of a chained redirect loop
description: This means that the URL is question is part of a redirect chain which results in a redirect loop (e.g. URL 1 -> URL -> 2 -> URL 3 -> URL 1), which results in the page being inaccessible.

title: Internal redirects from trailing slash mismatch
description: This means that the URL in question is redirected to another internal URL, where the only difference between URLs is the presence/absence of a trailing slash.

title: Internal redirects from case normalization
description: This means that the URL in question is redirected to another internal URL, where the only difference between URLs is a change of case to at least one of the characters (typically, an upper case character changed to lower case).

title: Internal redirected URLs
description: This means that the URL in question is redirected to another internal URL.

title: Redirected page resource URLs
description: This means that the URL in question is a resource URL that redirects to another URL.
note: redirect-resource-chain warns on multi-hop resource chains from the rendered asset data; not measured under --no-cwv.

title: External redirected URLs
description: This means that the URL in question is an external URL that redirects to another external URL.
note: Insight-level; external redirects are traversed but not reported as such.

title: Redirects using a Meta refresh
description: This means that the URL in question uses a meta refresh to redirect the page.

title: Broken internal URLs
description: This means that the URL in question was not successfully audited, and had a crawl status of either Not Found, Error, Forbidden or Timeout.

title: URL contains upper case characters
description: This means that the URL in question contains upper case characters.

title: URL contains whitespace
description: This means that the URL in question contains whitespace characters in the path.

title: Query string contains session ID parameters
description: This means that the URL in question contains a query string with parameters that are typically used as session IDs.

title: Query string contains tracking parameters
description: This means that the URL in question contains a query string with parameters that are typically used for tracking.

title: Query string contains a question mark
description: This means that the URL in question contains more than one question mark in the URL path.

title: Query string contains repetitive parameters
description: This means that the URL in question contains a query string with the same parameter more than once.

title: URL contains a double slash
description: This means that the URL in question contains a double slash in the path.

title: URL contains non-ASCII characters
description: This means that the URL in question contains characters outside the ASCII set.

title: URL contains repetitive elements
description: This means that the URL in question contains repetitive elements in the URL path.

title: URL contains more than one Google Tag Manager code
description: This means that the URL in question contains more than one Google Tag Manager snippet.

title: URL contains more than one Google Analytics code
description: This means that the URL in question contains multiple Google Analytics snippets.

title: Query string contains more than three parameters
description: This means that the URL in question contains a query string with more than 3 parameters.

title: Query string contains paginated parameters
description: This means that the URL in question contains a query string with apparent pagination parameters.
note: Pagination via rel=next/prev is checked; param-based pagination (?page=2) is not identified as such.

title: Query string contains search or filter parameters
description: URLs that contain a query string with apparent search or filter parameters (e.g. http://example.com/search?w=shoes).
note: Internal search URLs are detected; filter parameters are not.

title: Query string contains sort parameters
description: This means that the URL in question contains a query string with apparent sort parameters.
note: Insight-level; sort params counted but not classified.

title: URL contains no Google Tag Manager code
description: This means that the URL in question does not contain the Google Tag Manager snippet.
note: Analytics presence is not an SEO issue; deliberately out of scope.

title: URL contains no Google Analytics code
description: This means that the URL in question does not contain the Google Analytics snippet.
note: Same as above.

title: Canonicalized URL received organic search traffic
description: This means that the URL in question is canonicalized to another URL, yet received organic search traffic, per the connected Google Analytics and Google Search Console accounts.
note: Requires Google Search Console / GA4 integration, which the CLI does not have.

title: Disallowed URL received organic search traffic
description: This means that the URL in question is disallowed in robots.txt, yet received organic search traffic, per the connected Google Analytics and Google Search Console accounts.
note: Requires GSC/GA4.

title: Forbidden (403) URL received search traffic
description: This means that the URL in question returns a HTTP status of 403 (Forbidden), yet received organic search traffic, per the connected Google Analytics and Google Search Console accounts.
note: Requires GSC/GA4.

title: Noindex URL received organic search traffic
description: This means that the URL in question is noindex, yet received organic search traffic, per the connected Google Analytics and Google Search Console accounts.
note: Requires GSC/GA4.

title: Not Found (4XX) URL received search traffic
description: This means that the URL in question returns a HTTP status of 4XX, yet received organic search traffic, per the connected Google Analytics and Google Search Console accounts.
note: Requires GSC/GA4.

title: Redirect (3XX) URL received organic search traffic
description: This means that the URL in question returns a HTTP status of 3XX (Redirect), yet received organic search traffic, per the connected Google Analytics and Google Search Console accounts.
note: Requires GSC/GA4.

title: Orphan URL received search traffic
description: This means that the URL in question is not part of the crawlable website architecture, yet received organic search traffic, per the connected Google Analytics and Google Search Console accounts.
note: Requires GSC/GA4.

title: Had bounce rate greater than or equal to 80%
description: This means that the URL in question received organic search traffic with a bounce rate of 80% or more - with data taken from the connected Google Analytics account.
note: Requires GA4. GA4 also no longer reports bounce rate in this form.

title: Error (5XX) URL in XML Sitemaps
description: This means that the URL in question returns an HTTP 'Error' status (5XX), yet is included in an XML Sitemap.
note: Crawl mode only: sitemap URLs cross-referenced with crawled status codes.

title: Noindex URL in XML Sitemaps
description: This means that the URL in question is noindex, yet is included in an XML Sitemap.

title: Not Found (4XX) URL in XML Sitemaps
description: This means that the URL in question returns a HTTP status of 4XX, yet is included in an XML Sitemap.

title: Canonicalized URL in XML Sitemaps
description: This means that the URL in question has a canonical element that points to another URL, yet is included in an XML Sitemap.
note: Crawl mode only: canonical state per sitemap URL.

title: Disallowed URL in XML Sitemaps
description: This means that the URL in question is disallowed in robots.txt, yet is included in an XML Sitemap.
note: Crawl mode only: per-URL robots.txt disallow flags from the crawl.

title: Forbidden (403) URL in XML Sitemaps
description: This means that the URL in question returns a HTTP status of 403 (Forbidden), yet is included in an XML Sitemap.

title: Redirect (3XX) URL in XML Sitemaps
description: This means that the URL in question returns an HTTP 'Redirect' status (3XX), yet is included in an XML Sitemap.
note: 3xx sitemap URLs warn rather than fail.

title: Timed out URL in XML Sitemaps
description: This means that the URL in question returns timed out when reference catalog requested it, yet is included in an XML Sitemap.
note: Timeouts (statusCode 0) warn rather than fail.

title: URL in multiple XML Sitemaps
description: This means that the URL in question is included in more than one XML Sitemap.
note: Within-document duplicates and cross-sitemap membership both checked.

title: Mixed content (loads HTTP resources on HTTPS URL)
description: This means that the URL in question is loaded over a secure HTTPS protocol, but some other resources (such as images, videos, stylesheets, scripts) are loaded over an insecure HTTP connection.

title: Internal HTTP URLs
description: This means that the URL in question is loaded over an insecure HTTP connection.

title: HTTPS URL links to an HTTP URL
description: This means that the URL in question uses the HTTPS protocol, but contains outgoing links to internal URLs which are on HTTP.

title: HTTP URL contains a password input field
description: This means that the URL in question uses the HTTP protocol, but contains a form with a password input field.

title: HTTPS URL contains a form posting to HTTP
description: This means that the URL in question uses the HTTPS protocol, but contains a form that posts to a HTTP URL.

title: Loads page resources using protocol relative URIs
description: This means that the URL in question loads in resources using protocol relative URLs, which can be requested over HTTP and as such represent a security vulnerability.

title: Invalid incoming hreflang annotations
description: This means that the URL in question has one or more incoming hreflang annotation that is invalid (e.g. invalid language or region code).
note: Crawl mode only for the incoming side: annotations from other crawled pages targeting this URL are code-validated.

title: Has invalid outgoing hreflang annotations
description: This means that the URL in question has one or more outgoing hreflang annotation that is invalid (e.g. invalid language or region code).
note: Language/region codes are validated against ISO 639-1 / 3166-1.

title: Has outgoing hreflang annotations to noindex URLs
description: This means that the URL in question has at least one outgoing hreflang annotation URL which is noindex.
note: Crawl mode only: reads hreflang target robots state from SiteContext.pages.

title: Noindex URL has incoming hreflang
description: This means that the URL in question is defined as a hreflang alternate, yet is noindex.

title: Has outgoing hreflang annotations to broken URLs
description: This means that the URL in question has at least one outgoing hreflang annotation which returned as Not Found (4XX) or Error (5XX).
note: Static malformed-URL checks plus crawl-mode live check: 4xx/5xx fail, fetch timeouts warn.

title: Has outgoing hreflang annotations to canonicalized URLs
description: This means that the URL in question has at least one outgoing hreflang annotation which is canonicalized to another URL.

title: Canonicalized URL has incoming hreflang
description: This means that the URL in question is defined as a hreflang alternate, yet is canonicalized to another URL.
note: Outgoing direction covered; "this page is canonicalized and is an hreflang target" needs crawl-level data.

title: Has outgoing hreflang annotations to disallowed URLs
description: This means that the URL in question has at least one outgoing hreflang annotation URL that is disallowed in robots.txt.
note: Crawl mode only: cross-references hreflang targets against robots.txt disallows.

title: Disallowed URL has incoming hreflang
description: This means that the URL in question is defined as a hreflang alternate, yet is disallowed in robots.txt.
note: Crawl mode only: checks the site-wide hreflang graph against this page's disallow flag.

title: Has conflicting incoming hreflang annotations
description: This means that the URL in question has multiple, different incoming hreflang annotations.
note: Crawl mode only: compares what other crawled pages say about this URL; x-default excluded.

title: Has conflicting outgoing hreflang annotations
description: This means that the URL in question has one or more outgoing hreflang annotations that specify the same URL, but with different hreflang - so there is a conflict between the two annotations.

title: Has multiple self-referencing hreflang annotations
description: This means that the URL in question has one or more self-referenced hreflang annotations, that specify different hreflang values - so there is a conflict between the annotations.

title: Has outgoing hreflang annotation to multiple URLs
description: This means that the URL in question has hreflang annotations that specify the same hreflang to multiple different URLs - so there is a conflict between the various annotations.

title: Has outgoing hreflang annotations using relative URLs
description: This means that the URL in question has hreflang annotations that have at least one outgoing hreflang annotation which is referenced as a relative URL.

title: Invalid HTML lang attribute
description: This means that the URL in question has defined the language/region attribute using HTML lang, but either the language code or the geography code is invalid (or both are invalid).

title: Mismatched hreflang and HTML lang declarations
description: This means that the URL in question has hreflang annotations and HTML lang attributes that do not match.

title: Missing hreflang annotations
description: This means that the URL in question is not specified as a translation through hreflang annotations.
note: Presence is checked, but we do not infer that a site should have hreflang (multilingual signals).

title: Missing reciprocal hreflang (no return-tag)
description: This means that the URL in question has hreflang annotations where at least one of the alternate hreflang URLs does not reciprocate.
note: Crawl mode only for true reciprocity: crawled targets must annotate this page in return; uncrawled targets skipped.

title: Has outgoing hreflang annotations to redirecting URLs
description: This means that the URL in question has at least one outgoing hreflang annotation which is redirected to another URL.
note: HTTP-on-HTTPS heuristic plus crawl-mode live check for actual 3xx responses.

title: Has unsupported or misconfigured hreflang
description: This means that the URL in question has one or more outgoing hreflang annotation that is configured incorrectly.

title: Has hreflang annotations using multiple methods
description: This means that the URL in question has hreflang annotations defined using more than one method (HTML, HTTP Header or XML Sitemap)
note: HTML vs HTTP header covered; XML sitemap method not parsed.

title: Missing canonical URL
description: This means that the URL in question hashreflang annotations, but no canonical tag.

title: Missing HTML lang attribute
description: This means that the URL in question has not defined the language/region attribute using HTML lang.

title: Has hreflang annotations without HTML lang
description: This means that the URL in question has hreflang annotations, but has not defined the language/region attribute using HTML lang.

title: Hreflang annotation also x-default
description: This means that the URL in question is defined as an hreflang alternate, and also defined as the x-default hreflang.

title: AMP Page has validation errors
description: This means that the URL in question is an AMP Page URL that contains validation errors and does not pass an AMP validation test.
note: AMP is deprecated as a ranking concern (page experience update 2021+; Google killed AMP cache requirement). Recommend not implementing.

title: AMP Page URL has canonical URL which is Error (5XX)
description: This means that the URL in question is an AMP Page URL, and contains a canonical tag which returned Error (5XX).
note: AMP-specific; see amp-page-has-validation-errors.

title: AMP Page URL has canonical URL which is Forbidden (403)
description: This means that the URL in question is an AMP Page URL, and contains a canonical tag which returned Forbidden (403).
note: AMP-specific.

title: AMP Page URL has canonical URL which is Not Found (4XX)
description: This means that the URL in question is an AMP Page URL, and contains a canonical tag which returned Not Found (4XX).
note: AMP-specific.

title: AMP Page URL is Error (5XX)
description: This means that the URL in question is an AMP Page URL, which returned Error (5XX).
note: AMP-specific.

title: AMP Page URL is Forbidden (403)
description: This means that the URL in question is an AMP Page URL which is Forbidden (403).
note: AMP-specific.

title: AMP Page URL is Not Found (4XX)
description: This means that the URL in question is an AMP Page URL, which is Not Found (4XX).
note: AMP-specific.

title: AMP Page URL has canonical URL which is canonicalized
description: This means that the URL in question is an AMP Page URL, and contains a canonical tag pointing to a canonicalized URL (i.e. the canonical URL is itself canonicalized to another URL).
note: AMP-specific.

title: AMP Page URL has canonical URL which is disallowed
description: This means that the URL in question is an AMP Page URL, and contains a canonical tag pointing to a disallowed URL.
note: AMP-specific.

title: AMP Page URL has canonical URL which is noindex
description: This means that the URL in question is an AMP Page URL, and contains a canonical tag pointing to a noindex URL.
note: AMP-specific.

title: AMP Page URL has canonical URL which is not indexable
description: This means that the URL in question is an AMP Page URL, and contains a canonical tag pointing to a URL which is not indexable.
note: AMP-specific.

title: AMP Page URL has canonical URL which is Redirect (3XX)
description: This means that the URL in question is an AMP Page URL, and contains a canonical tag which returned Redirect (3XX).
note: AMP-specific.

title: AMP Page URL is disallowed
description: This means that the URL in question is an AMP Page URL, which is disallowed in robots.txt.
note: AMP-specific.

title: AMP Page URL is missing a canonical tag
description: This means that the URL in question is an AMP Page URL, which does not contain a canonical tag.
note: AMP-specific.

title: AMP Page URL is missing the <html amp> tag
description: This means that the URL in question is an AMP Page URL, which does not contain an \<html amp> tag.
note: AMP-specific.

title: AMP Page URL is noindex
description: This means that the URL in question is an AMP Page URL, which is noindex.
note: AMP-specific.

title: AMP Page URL is Redirect (3XX)
description: This means that the URL in question is an AMP Page URL, which is a Redirect (3XX).
note: AMP-specific.

title: amphtml link only found in rendered DOM
description: This means that the URL in question has a an amphtml link element which is only present in the rendered DOM, and is not present in the source HTML.
note: AMP-specific.

title: AMP Page URL loops
description: This means that the URL in question contains an \<amphtml> tag pointing at a URL, where this URL also has \<amphtml> tag, that points back at the original URL.
note: AMP-specific.

title: URLs with duplicate content
description: This means that the URL in question has identical HTML content to at least one other indexable URL.

title: URLs with duplicate page titles
description: This means that the URL in question has the exact same page title as at least one other indexable URL.

title: Technically duplicate URLs
description: This means that the URL in question is technically identical to at least one other indexable URL. This could be URLs that are only different based on case, or have the same query string parameters and values (but in a different order).
note: We check the individual URL properties but do not cluster URLs that resolve to identical content.

title: URLs with duplicate title and meta descriptions
description: This means that the URL in question has the exact same page title and meta description as at least one other indexable URL.
note: The combination is implied by the two single-field rules.

title: URLs with similar content
description: This means that the URL in question has substantially similar HTML content to at least one other indexable URL.

title: URLs with duplicate h1s
description: This means that the URL in question has the exact same header 1 (h1) tag as at least one other indexable URL.
note: Crawl mode only: compares H1 text across SiteContext.pages.

title: URLs with duplicate meta descriptions
description: This means that the URL in question has the exact same meta description as at least one other indexable URL.

title: Multiple viewport <meta> tags were found in the <head>
description: This means that the URL in question contains multiple viewport \<meta> tags in the \<head>.

title: Content does not size correctly to viewport
description: This means that the URL in question is not responsive, and the page content does not size accordingly when the screen size is changed.
note: Static heuristics only; a true rendered-viewport overflow measurement would need a mobile render pass.

title: Font size is too small for mobile devices
description: This means that the URL in question contains some text which is too small, and therefore not legible for mobile devices.

title: Has one or more image-map <map> tags
description: This means that the URL in question contains image-map tags.

title: Tap targets are too small and close
description: This means that the URL in question contains touch targets (such as buttons and links) which are too small and close to each other.

title: Missing Viewport <Meta> tag in the <head> -reference catalog SEO Tips
description: This means that the URL in question does not contain a viewport \<meta> tag in the \<head>

title: The viewport <meta> tag does not have a width set
description: This means that the URL in question contains a viewport \<meta> tag with no width set.

title: The viewport <meta> tag has a specific width set
description: This means that the URL in question contains a viewport \<meta> tag with a specific width set.

title: The viewport <meta> tag has a maximum-scale set
description: This means that the URL in question contains a viewport \<meta> tag with a maximum-scale set.

title: The viewport <meta> tag has a minimum-scale set
description: This means that the URL in question contains a viewport \<meta> tag with a minimum-scale set.

title: The viewport <meta> tag initial-scale is incorrect
description: This means that the URL in question contains a viewport \<meta> tag with an initial-scale set to a value other than 1.0.

title: The viewport <meta> tag is missing an initial-scale
description: This means that the URL in question contains a viewport \<meta> tag with no initial-scale attribute.

title: The viewport <meta> tag prevents the user from scaling
description: This means that the URL in question contains a viewport \<meta> tag with the attribute user-scalable set to '0' or 'no', which prevents the user from zooming in or zooming out.

title: Eliminate render blocking resources
description: This means that the URL in question contains JavaScript or CSS that blocks the initial render of the page.

title: Avoid enormous network payloads
description: This means that the URL has an extremely large page size (over 4Mb), which makes it slow to download.

title: Serve static assets with an efficient cache policy
description: This means that the URL in question contains resource URLs, such as images or JavaScript files, which do not specify a cache header.
note: Per-asset cache headers from the Playwright render; not measured under --no-cwv.

title: Efficiently encode images
description: This means that the URL contains images that are unoptimized.
note: perf-image-encoding measures transferred bytes per rendered image; not measured under --no-cwv.

title: Defer offscreen images
description: This means that the URL contains images that are fully loaded by the browser even though they are not visible in the user's viewport.

title: Minify JavaScript
description: This means that the URL in question contains JavaScript files that are not minified or could be minified further.
note: Inline JS checked directly; large external scripts without a .min. URL marker flagged heuristically from render asset data (bodies not captured).

title: Minify CSS
description: This means that the URL in question contains CSS files that are not minified or could be minified further.
note: Inline CSS checked directly; large external stylesheets without a .min. URL marker flagged heuristically from render asset data (bodies not captured).

title: Reduce server response times (TTFB)
description: This means that the URL in question has a Time-to-First-Byte (TTFB) greater than 600ms.

title: Enable text compression
description: This means that the URL in question contains text-based resources that are not served with compression.
note: perf-asset-compression checks sub-resource compression from render asset data; not measured under --no-cwv.

title: Ensure text remains visible during webfont load
description: This means that the URL in question hides text content until the webfont loads, causing a flash of invisible text.

title: Add dimensions to images
description: This means that the URL contains images that do not have width and height size attributes.

title: Properly size images
description: This means that the URL contains images that are larger than the size they are rendered at.
note: Rendered-size vs intrinsic-size comparison needs layout measurement.

title: Remove unused CSS
description: This means that the URL contains 'unused CSS', which is not actually used for rendering.
note: Needs CSS coverage collection; planned as perf-unused-css in the Lighthouse PRD Phase 3 but not yet implemented.

title: Reduce Or Remove Unused JavaScript for SEO - reference catalog SEO Tips
description: This means that the URL contains 'unused JavaScript', which is not actually used for rendering.
note: Needs JS coverage collection; planned as perf-unused-js in the Lighthouse PRD Phase 3 but not yet implemented.

title: Transferred image size is over 100KB
description: This means that the URL in question is an image file that is over 100KB, which is generally considered large.
note: perf-image-encoding measures content-length per rendered image against a 100KB threshold; not measured under --no-cwv.

title: Serve images in next gen formats
description: This means that the URL contains images that are in older formats (BMP, JPEG or PNG).

title: Use video formats for animated content
description: This means that the URL contains animated content in GIF format.

title: Avoid excessive DOM width
description: This means that the URL in question has a parent node in the DOM with more than the recommended 60 child nodes.

title: Avoid excessive DOM size
description: This means that the URL in question has more than the recommended 1500 elements in the DOM.

title: Avoid excessive DOM depth
description: This means that the URL in question has DOM nodes exceeding the maximum recommended depth of 32.

title: Noindex only in the HTTP response HTML
description: This means that the URL in question contains a noindex in the response HTML, and not in the rendered HTML.

title: Nofollow only in the HTTP response HTML
description: This means that the URL in question contains a nofollow in the response HTML, and not in the rendered HTML.

title: Canonical only in the rendered HTML
description: This means that the URL in question contains a canonical element that is only present in the rendered HTML and is not present in the initial response HTML. The canonical is only present on the page once the page is rendered.

title: Canonical mismatch between rendered and response HTML
description: This means that the URL in question contains a canonical element has a different link in the response HTML, when compared with the rendered HTML.

title: Page Title only in the rendered HTML
description: This means that the URL in question has a page title that is not present in the response HTML of the page, it only appears after JavaScript has executed.

title: Page Title modified by JavaScript
description: This means that the URL in question has a page title that is different in the response HTML of the page, when compared with the rendered HTML.

title: Meta Description only in the rendered HTML
description: This means that the URL in question has a meta description that is not present in the response HTML of the page, it only appears after JavaScript has executed.

title: Meta Description modified by JavaScript
description: This means that the URL in question has a meta description that is different in the response HTML of the page, when compared with the rendered HTML.

title: <h1> only in the rendered HTML
description: This means that the URL in question has an \<h1> that is not present in the response HTML of the page, it only appears after JavaScript has executed.

title: <h1> modified by JavaScript
description: This means that the URL in question has an \<h1> that is different in the response HTML of the page, when compared with the rendered HTML.

title: Contains JavaScript content
description: This means that the URL in question contains body content that is only discovered after JavaScript has executed: the content is not present in the response HTML of the page.

title: Contains JavaScript links
description: This means that the URL in question contains links that are only discovered after JavaScript has executed: the links are not present in the response HTML of the page.
